title: Why does my video wait before it plays?
fullTitle: Your MP4 May Wait to Play: The Index Is at the End

scenes.narration: You put an MP4 on your website, and it seems to wait before it plays. Is the file the problem? An MP4 is a list of boxes. So we will not guess. We will read the order of the boxes.
captions: An MP4 that seems to wait before it plays.
Read the order of the boxes.

scenes.narration: Here is a synthetic clip: ten seconds, six forty by three sixty, with a tone. We encode it twice. Once with the plain command. Once with dash movflags plus faststart. The picture is the same. Two hundred fifty frames, both times.

Now read the top level boxes. The plain file goes: ftyp, free, mdat, moov. The mdat box holds the picture and the sound. The moov box is the index: the duration, and where every frame lives. Here it comes last, at byte nine hundred seventeen thousand of a nine hundred twenty seven thousand byte file.
captions: The index (moov) is the last box.

scenes.narration: With plus faststart, the order is ftyp, moov, free, mdat. Same size. Same frames. The index moved to the front. Two separate readers agree on this: a parser we wrote, and ffprobe's own trace. Two ffmpeg builds gave the same order.
captions: Same size, same frames. The index moved.

scenes.narration: Now a client. We serve both files from a local server and let ffprobe read them. A client that cannot seek has to read from the start. For the plain file, the server sent every byte. For the faststart file, under fifty thousand. A client that can ask for byte ranges copes with the plain file too, by jumping to the end. That took three requests, not one.
captions: No seeking: whole file vs under 50 KB.

scenes.narration: The flag is not free. The FFmpeg documentation says it runs a second pass, can take a while, and does not work in various situations, such as fragmented output. That is why it is off by default. And remember what we measured with: ffprobe as the client. We did not test a browser.
captions: FFmpeg docs: a second pass, can take a while.
Tested with ffprobe. Not tested: a browser.

scenes.narration: Check the box order before you upload. One flag moves the index to the front. Not tested here: browsers, other players, and fragmented MP4.
captions: Check the box order before you upload.
Not tested: browsers, other players, fragmented MP4.
